slides.reasoning: Design A delivers a bolder hierarchy with a hero $4.8M lockup, labeled data points and a dramatic glowing curve that fills the frame, while Design B leaves a large empty band at the bottom and a smaller, less commanding ARR statement.

Design A is a genuine illustrated journey with hand-drawn route marks, day markers, taped callout and buddy tag in the clay-dominant palette, whereas Design B inverts to a mostly empty blush field with a large dead zone and a stiff three-label curve.

Design A shows a real before/after diagram (tangled reconciliation vs. one identity graph) with a dominant $780k figure and disciplined rules, while Design B falls back on two plain boxes of bullet lists and a bottom row that reads as a generic stat strip.

Design A's orbital allocation ring with serif numerals, coral reserve arc and elegant leader lines matches the institutional brief precisely, while Design B's ordinary donut plus all-caps sans headline and paired stat grid feels less restrained and adds off-palette sage.

Design A makes the product the hero with an exploded technical render, precise callouts and keynote-scale ARC ONE lockup, whereas Design B centers a small boxed stock-style photo with four symmetrical labels and awkward right-aligned text.

Design A's coherent chart system, variance markers, scorecard rows and emphasized activation gap are cleanly spaced, while Design B has a colliding '103% of plan' label overlapping the plan line and a heavy orange bar that unbalances the composition.

Design A builds a true transit-map strategy diagram with converging lines and an interchange node carrying the north-star measures, while Design B's four parallel bars with labels squeezed between lines create ambiguous label-to-line association and a large empty midsection.

Design A's chevron swimlanes, week ruler, gate diamonds and rollout bars are precisely aligned with ownership noted, whereas Design B has gate text overlapping the dashed gridlines and the Gate C label colliding with the diamond and bars.

Design A presents a bold 4C loop with marker annotations, an annotated worked example and a strong practice-rule footer, while Design B duplicates quote marks ('""'), leaves the entire lower-right quadrant empty, and has connector dots crossing its own label text.

Design A's unit-square 68% chart, illustrated three-app journey with confidence-break annotations and pull-quote form a memorable editorial spread, while Design B's stacked app boxes and cramped headline wrap deliver less narrative clarity.

Design A achieves the auditorium keynote moment with an oversized dissolving wordmark, elegant visible/hidden UI diagram and audience silhouette, while Design B relies on generic dark stock imagery, plain outlined boxes and an awkward orphaned 'it?' in the provocation block.

Design A's oversized editorial numerals, customer quote panel and numbered 90-day priorities fill the split composition with confident rhythm, whereas Design B leaves roughly a third of the orange field empty and drops the closing line into a cramped sidebar.

Design A makes the corridor map the emotional centerpiece with secured/remaining parcels, scale bar, river labels and a taped field ledger, while Design B reduces the map to a schematic band and leaves a large empty area under the copy.

Design A's enormous annotated 'a' with yellow counter, baseline/x-height rules and three specimen comparisons is genuinely instructional, while Design B's smaller letterform has crossing leader lines and an 'aperture' pointer landing on the baseline rather than the aperture.

Design A's collage citrus macro, sector bar and dotted partnership-moment ledger create an energetic editorial composition, while Design B suffers broken letterspacing in its tag labels ('FUT URE T ABLE ST AGE') and a sizable empty region mid-slide.
